problem_statement: The robin-dela/hover-effect demo page is a live WebGL hover-transition gallery: a balloon carousel with PREVIOUS/NEXT controls sits above a grid of six hoverEffect shader demos (a video transition, three still-image shaders including the New York and ice hovers, the MY BUTTON displacement demo, and a submit displacement demo), all driven by the bundled dist/hover-effect.umd.js and local textures under images/. Rework the demo's own Shader gallery browsing experience: keep every WebGL canvas, the balloon carousel, and MY BUTTON fully interactive, and repair the Shader gallery filter bar that sits above the demo grid. The filter bar offers category tabs (All shaders / Video / Stills / Displacement) that filter the real demo cards and a live readout that must report the visible count as 'Showing N of 6 . <Category>'. The reference filter bar wraps cleanly on a phone, keeps the active tab legible, lays the filtered demo cards out without collision, stamps a gallery-filter--<category> modifier class on the bar for each chosen category, and recomputes the live readout on every click. Fix the mobile horizontal overflow of the tab row, the colliding/illegible filtered grid, the missing per-category state, and the stale readout so all four browsing dimensions hold while the original canvases keep rendering.
required_content: Keep the hover-effect demo runnable from the existing root page with the top balloon WebGL carousel, PREVIOUS and NEXT buttons, video transition canvas, New York hover canvas, ice/ramen hover canvas, hover text canvas, MY BUTTON canvas, submit canvas, bundled images, bundled videos, the existing bundled UMD script loaded by the page, and existing package build intact.

Add a browser-visible workflow panel near the carousel and demo grid that contains the exact text Hover transition workflow, Balloon carousel state: ready, Hover shader previews: waiting for canvas hover, Displacement texture stack: stripe, ramen, fluid, and dot, and Asset samples: balloon.jpg, ny.jpg, stripe1mul.png.

Use real local img elements inside the workflow panel for images/balloon.jpg, images/ny.jpg, and images/stripe1mul.png with the exact alt text Balloon carousel source, New York hover source, and Stripe displacement texture; do not replace them with remote assets, data URIs, CSS-only backgrounds, or generated screenshots.

Wire the existing PREVIOUS and NEXT controls so the panel reports Balloon carousel state: previous frame requested and Balloon carousel state: next frame requested after the existing hoverEffect carousel methods run.

Wire at least the New York hover demo so hovering the original canvas area updates the panel to Hover shader previews: New York transition active without disabling the original WebGL hover transition.

Style the panel as a compact component that matches the sparse black-white example page: restrained typography, thin borders, stable asset thumbnails, concise status cells, no marketing hero, and no horizontal overflow on desktop, tablet, or mobile.
design_constraints: Preserve the demo-first character of the page: the WebGL canvases must remain the primary visual surfaces, and the workflow panel should clarify them rather than replacing them with a static gallery.

Keep the implementation dependency-free and localized to the existing demo page unless a small helper is unavoidable; do not rewrite the bundled hoverEffect library output, change the package build, introduce a router, or swap the gallery into a framework page.
Use stable responsive CSS with explicit max widths, grid tracks, and fixed thumbnail aspect ratios so the status text, chips, images, and canvases do not resize or overlap unpredictably.

The visual language should stay close to the original example: white page, black controls, thin neutral borders, compact uppercase labels, and local image evidence rather than decorative gradients or oversized hero sections.
Do not rename the project, delete original examples, remove PREVIOUS/NEXT, remove MY BUTTON, remove any local canvas asset references, or convert the WebGL demos into plain image cards.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial protect the original canvas-heavy demo page, top carousel, controls, and responsive layout before task-specific actions are inspected.

desktop_workflow_panel, tablet_workflow_panel, and mobile_workflow_panel inspect the new workflow component and its local asset thumbnails across viewport sizes without requiring the baseline to contain that selector.
desktop_next_carousel and desktop_previous_carousel click the existing controls and verify the workflow status changes while the carousel action remains executable.
desktop_hover_ny hovers the original New York WebGL demo and verifies the panel receives a hover-state update without replacing the canvas.
mobile_next_carousel clicks the existing NEXT control on a narrow viewport to protect the mobile carousel workflow and responsive status text.

change_completion: The workflow panel contains the required exact status, texture-stack, and asset-sample text, and the click/hover states update the panel with the required dynamic messages.
The panel uses real local img elements for balloon.jpg, ny.jpg, and stripe1mul.png with meaningful alt text so browser captures can verify asset grounding.
design_consistency: The panel follows the original hover-effect demo's sparse black-white style, thin borders, compact labels, and canvas-first composition.
The change clarifies the existing WebGL workflow instead of converting the page into a marketing hero, static image gallery, or unrelated dashboard.
responsive: Desktop and tablet states keep the workflow panel, chips, thumbnails, and canvas grid stable without document-width overflow.
Mobile states collapse the panel and thumbnails cleanly while keeping PREVIOUS/NEXT usable and the canvases visible.
regression: The existing PREVIOUS/NEXT controls, MY BUTTON text, hoverEffect canvas instances, local image paths, video paths, and bundled script loading remain intact.
Hovering the New York demo and clicking carousel controls still execute against the original component surfaces rather than only changing static text.

metadata.design_goal: complete or refine a user workflow across one or more meaningful screens
metadata.source_repo_kind: Standalone WebGL hoverEffect example page with bundled images, videos, displacement textures, carousel controls, and multiple canvas demos
metadata.selected_repo_reason: Unused runnable interactive-canvas candidate whose baseline already exposes real WebGL hover surfaces and local image/texture assets, making it suitable for a component-level experience-continuity modification.

author_notes: Slot slot_282 targets interactive_canvas / experience_continuity / modify / component / L3. The task turns the sparse hover-effect example into a testable workflow experience by adding status feedback, local asset evidence, and responsive explanatory structure while protecting the original WebGL carousel and hover demos.
